review_candidates.title: 23438 Finance Officer (Migrant Protection, Return and Reintegration Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa (MPRR-SSA))
review_candidates.description: Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Regional Director – Management (DRD-M) in Dakar, and the direct supervision of the Project Finance and Budget Officer – Migrant Protection, Return and Reintegration Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa (MPRR-SSA) in close coordination with the Senior Regional Programme Coordinator (MPRR-SSA), the Finance Officer (MPRR-SSA) will assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) in the programmes budget, accounts, and financial reports of all the implementing Country Offices (COs), provide support to the programmatic unit of the MPRR-SSA team in the areas of financial monitoring and reporting. The Finance Officer (MPRR-SSA) will work closely with the European Commission Compliance Unit in IOM Global Office Brussels, Regional Office, as well as central units at Headquarters (HQ). The MPRR-SSA is an EU-funded programme that is implemented in 16 countries of sub-Saharan Africa, including Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Cameroon, Chad, Ethiopia, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal, Somalia, and Sudan. Responsibilities Assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) to monitor and oversee the financial management of all activities, including oversight of financial expenditure and accountability, and undertake financial analysis of all activities in the offices implementing the MPRR-SSA programme. Assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) to oversee and coordinate the preparation and review of EU financial reports in accordance with IOM regulations and EU regulations and established procedures. In coordination with the Senior Regional Programme Coordinator (MPRR-SSA), Project Managers, the Regional Office (RO) Coordination Unit, Global Office Brussels, and Resources Management Officers (RMOs), prepare budget reports, proposals, and revisions in the Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA). Contribute to the budget control process and analyse variances between the budget and actual expenditures for MPRR-SSA projects. Contribute to the creation of draft general instructions and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure compliance with the general instructions of IOM and relevant permanent instructions in the areas of general administration, finance, Supply Chain, Information and Communications Technology (ICT), and Human Resources (HR). Contribute to the capacity building initiatives to train local staff on EU and IOM’s administrative/financial policies and procedures. As assigned by the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA), undertake travel to offices in view to building financial management capacity of administrative and finance staff in the field. Provide support to the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) in facilitating the financial audit of the MPRR-SSA programme in accordance with the donor agreements. Assess monthly financial reports and advise on resolving anomalies and unusual trends. Provide advice and guidance to Country Offices (COs) in the Region with management of implementing Partners (IP) under the MPRR-SSA programme. Contribute to ensure compliance with all administrative and financial rules, instructions, regulations, and procedures related to the EU-funded project(s). In coordination with the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) and upon approval of the Regional Financial Comptroller, undertake duty travel to the CO to increase capacity building in financial reporting in relation to assigned projects. Perform other duties as may be assigned. Required Qualifications And Experience Education Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Auditing, or related fields from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or, University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Experience in accounting, financial management and reporting; Experience in preparing clear and concise financial and management reports; Experience working in and with international institutions; Experience with internal control assessment, internal or external audit; Previous work experience in the region is an advantage; Previous working experience in emergency operations is an advantage; and, Experience with EU budgeting rules is mandatory. Skills Knowledge of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS); Knowledge of the IOM/UN accounting system, software, and procedures, Common System regulations, policies, and procedures is a distinct advantage; Familiarity with financial oversight and public administration is an advantage; and, Knowledge of MS Office products and good computer literacy skills are required. Languages For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written). Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage. Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. How to apply Internationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months. Appointment will be subject to all clearances, including medical and security and as well as accreditation, and any residency or visa requirements. Vacancies close at 23:59 local time in Geneva, Switzerland on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted. IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and any forms of discrimination. IOM is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children. IOM conducts reference checks and background verification, including through system-wide databases such as ClearCheck, to help ensure that candidates have no record of misconduct, including on sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, or fraud. Candidates are expected to uphold these standards and principles at all times. IOM does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process—whether for application, interview, processing, training, or otherwise—and does not request any information related to bank accounts. IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM WAVE system (for internal candidates, link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. review_candidates.title: Customer Support Engineer
review_candidates.description: This is a Fully Remote Job About Our Client: Coursedog operates in the higher education technology space, addressing challenges related to outdated academic systems that hinder student success. The organization provides an Intelligent Academic Operations Platform used by over 400 colleges and universities, serving more than 3.3 million students. The platform integrates academic scheduling, curriculum and catalog management, assessment, and workflow automation to help institutions reduce administrative obstacles and improve education delivery. About the Opportunity: The CUSTOMER SUPPORT ENGINEER role is dedicated to managing and resolving technical support issues for higher education institutions using the platform. This position is responsible for investigating and troubleshooting configuration, data, and integration challenges, ensuring timely and effective resolution to maintain mission-critical academic operations. The role directly impacts customer satisfaction and system reliability by providing clear communication and thorough documentation throughout the support process. Responsibilities: Manage end-to-end resolution of support tickets within assigned coverage Investigate and resolve configuration, data, and integration issues for higher education clients Communicate proactively with customers regarding ticket status and resolution Reproduce issues to identify root causes before escalation Escalate complex cases promptly to technical or product teams Document troubleshooting steps and solutions for team reference Utilize AI-assisted tools and automation in daily workflows Incorporate quality assurance feedback for continuous improvement Requirements: 3 to 4 years of experience in SaaS technical support or similar customer-facing technical roles Proficient in managing caseloads within ticketing or CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce Service Cloud, Zendesk) under SLA requirements Ability to interpret browser console errors, network logs, and basic API responses Strong troubleshooting skills focused on root cause analysis Effective written communication for technical and non-technical audiences Good judgment in case ownership and escalation decisions Professional and calm demeanor when handling high-stakes or frustrated customers Collaborative and customer-oriented approach Pay Range and Compensation Package: Base salary range of $75,000 to $80,000, dependent on experience and qualifications Performance-based variable compensation component targeting total earnings of $83,000 to $88,000 upon achieving objectives Equal Opportunity Statement: Our client is an equal opportunity employer. They celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or national origin. Note: TalentHop is a recruitment partner of this role. Please note that all employment decisions, including candidate assessment, interviews, hiring, compensation, and employment terms, are made exclusively by the hiring employer.

review_candidates.title: Control Centre Operations Analyst
review_candidates.description: Era4 is supporting Valencia Energy with its continued growth and recruitment. Valencia Energy operates power generation, renewable energy and critical infrastructure assets across the UK, with a 24/7 Control Centre providing monitoring, incident management, security oversight and operational support to data centre clients. Working closely with Valencia, Era4 develops and operates renewable-powered AI infrastructure, transforming legacy industrial and energy sites into modern data-centre facilities. Control Centre Operations Analyst Location: Ardley, Oxfordshire (Valencia Control Centre) Shift Pattern: 4 on / 4 off rotating days and nights (24/7 operation) The Role We're looking for a proactive Control Centre Operations Analyst to join our 24/7 operations team. You will monitor and manage power generation assets and data centre operations, responding to alarms, coordinating incidents, supporting engineers, and ensuring high levels of asset performance, safety, and customer service. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with experience in control room, utilities, critical infrastructure, NOC, SOC, or operational monitoring environments. Key Responsibilities Operations & Monitoring Monitor and control operational assets, data centre alarms, performance KPIs and environmental conditions using SCADA and related systems. Respond to alarms, faults and operational incidents in real time, ensuring appropriate escalation. Coordinate call-outs and provide operational support to field engineering teams. Manage access control, CCTV and security incidents across operational and customer environments. Service & Incident Management Manage and triage tickets through Halo and other operational systems. Act as a key point of contact for customers and stakeholders. Provide timely incident updates, communications, and escalations. Coordinate with engineers, site teams, security providers, and third parties. Performance & Reporting Support asset optimisation, reliability, and continuous improvement initiatives. Maintain accurate operational, maintenance, and incident records. Produce operational reports and performance information. Support planning, compliance, and safety activities. Essential Skills & Experience Previous experience using SCADA, monitoring platforms, or similar operational systems. Ability to work independently and make decisions under pressure. Problem solving skills in a real time operational environment. Proactive approach with sound judgement and escalation awareness. Desirable Experience in power generation, utilities, critical infrastructure, data centres, NOC/SOC, or other 24/7 operations. Knowledge of alarm monitoring, incident management, or access control systems. Experience with CCTV, security monitoring, or access management platforms. IOSH or similar health & safety qualification. Experience with operational reporting and data analysis. Why Join Era4 You’ll be joining a mission-driven start-up building critical national infrastructure, where operational excellence directly enables growth. This role offers high visibility with leadership, real autonomy, and the chance to shape how a next-generation company operates at scale. Diversity & Inclusion Era4 is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.
